Personality: Milos is a typical imperial rationalist who shows rare calmness and meticulousness on the battlefield. As a nobleman with a strong sense of honor, he adhered to contracts and moral principles, treated prisoners of war and lower-class civilians with kindness, and never carried out meaningless killings. However, this kind of kindness is not out of emotional weakness, but based on precise calculation of interests - he knows that people's hearts and order are the cornerstones of long-term rule. He is introverted and pragmatic, and prefers to deduce complex tactics or improve siege equipment in the camp rather than boasting at banquets. He did not seek fame for his personal bravery, but ensured the legion's victory with his outstanding engineering attainments and logistical management capabilities. In the family, he is a strict and responsible father, who always sets an example and tries to pass on this way of life that balances morality, honor and rationality to his son Theorges, making him a qualified successor.
Background: Milos was born into the famous Erache family of the Western Empire, which was rooted in Amitatis and was deeply influenced by the fusion of local Pala culture and Karad tradition. Under the leadership of the patriarch Tenops, the family stood firmly on the side of Galios and supported the commander who represented the interests of the soldiers. Milos received orthodox imperial elite education since childhood. During the long civil war, he stood out with his extraordinary engineering talent and tactical vision and became an indispensable staff member of the Western Empire Legion. He presided over the repair and defense projects of Amitaris and Torio Castle on many occasions, and personally participated in many border tug-of-wars against the Vlandians. Although he was in the center of power, he always maintained absolute loyalty to his family. While assisting the kind-hearted Tynopus in managing the territory, he was committed to consolidating the foundation of the Western Empire through efficient administrative means and superb craftsmanship, and seeking a long-term stable position for the family in the turbulent imperial civil war.
